text:
marco: oddball report — our new monorepo starter (pnpm workspace) exhibits SDK parity weirdness: local Next server shows eval metrics & embeddings as expected, but the edge preview and the vignette app get different behaviours: missing telemetry + different eval response_format. seems like two different SDK versions are running even though package.json pins the same semver. :confused:

marco: repro steps I used:
1) pnpm -w install on repo `github.com/redwood/samples/mono-next-starter`
2) cd examples/mini-app && pnpm dev (uses next edge)
3) trigger eval/e mbeds from UI -> UI ok, Console shows zero evals and wrong structured output in ingestion tests

marco: digging into node_modules, `pnpm list @redwood/inference-js` shows two entries: one at root 0.12.3 and one under examples/mini-app 0.11.4. somehow the workspace resolves to the older version for the edge bundle.

viv: ah, pnpm hoisting + peer/workspace protocol quirks. older examples in samples were still using a local pinned copy in their package.json (not workspace:), so when building the edge route the bundler pulled the nested copy. Edge runtime used the package-bundled SDK. Node dev server used the root hoisted copy. explains parity differences.

adele: that would cause a ton of subtle issues — telemetry changes landed in 0.12 and eval param canonicalization in 0.12.1. If two SDKs are present you'll get mismatched request bodies and missing telemetry in runtime that bundles the old copy.

marco: I repro with `node -e "console.log(require.resolve('@redwood/inference-js'))"` run from root vs from examples/mini-app and got two different paths. confirmed.

viv: quick mitigation: add a workspace override in the monorepo root package.json using pnpm's overrides or use the workspace: protocol in all example package.jsons. Also add a preinstall script to detect duplicate versions and fail CI if found.

adele: for starters we should: 1) update examples to use `workspace:^` or `workspace:0.12.3` for @redwood/inference-js, 2) add a devex doc note about monorepo pitfalls and bundler behavior, 3) add a CI lint step `node tools/check-sdk-dedupe.js` that runs `pnpm -w list @redwood/inference-js --json` and errors if >1 distinct version seen.

marco: i pushed a tiny script that checks `require.resolve` across example workspaces and fails if paths differ. test: `node tools/check-sdk-dedupe.js` returns non-zero in my fork. opening PR shortly.

ci-bot: created issue #2010 (devex) "mono-next-starter: ensure single SDK version in pnpm workspace" — https://github.com/redwood/samples/issues/2010

buildsvc: note for infra — bundlers like Vercel's edge optimizer often bundle nested node_modules into the edge function. if you have multiple SDK copies the edge function may ship the older copy. We should add a recommended pattern in samples: rely on workspace: and pin the root devDependency.

viv: also adding runtime guard in the starter: at module init we call `const sdkPath = require.resolve('@redwood/inference-js'); if (sdkPath.includes('/node_modules/') && !sdkPath.startsWith(require.resolve('@redwood/inference-js', { paths: [process.cwd()] }).replace(/@redwood\/inference-js.*/, '@redwood/inference-js'))) console.warn('Multiple SDK copies detected. See devex/mono-sdk-dedupe docs');` — crude but helps catch during local dev.

adele: can we upstream a package `@redwood/dev-tools` with a check command `redwood-check sdk-dedupe` so starter authors can run it? would be handy. For now the script + CI check is enough.

marco: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/samples/pull/4122 "mono-next-starter: workspace pin for SDK, dedupe check, docs" — includes: workspace: pin, check script, CI job, and README blurb.

ci-bot: PR linked to issue #2010 and added to pipelines backlog.

viv: follow-up note: also audit other monorepo examples for stale package.json pins (search for @redwood/inference-js occurrences) — i found three. creating a sweep task.

marco: thanks everyone. learned the hard way: monorepo + pnpm requires workspace: protocol for shared SDKs or you'll get subtle runtime parity bugs. will follow up after PR merges to see if CI catches more forks. :thumbsup:
